subject: Merge ownership & secret access reconciliation for CAIQ intake
messages:
From: Alice Bryant <alice.bryant@finbank.org>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: security-assessor@finbank.org
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 12:12:00 -04:00
Subject: CAIQ intake — questions on merge ownership and secrets custody

Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick sync last week. As part of our CAIQ intake for Redwood we need a concise reconciliation of who (by role) is able to merge to protected branches and how secrets referenced by CI jobs are approved and rotated. Specifically we need:

- A one-page mapping of PR approvers -> repository/branch (who can merge vs who can approve).
- CI job owners and where their secrets live (vault path + last rotation).
- Audit evidence (logs) showing the last 30 days of vault read/write by CI service accounts.

Can you confirm whether Redwood has ephemeral CI tokens for merge gates and whether there is a canary/revert playbook tied to deployments? If you can attach the artifact list or a shared Drive link, that would speed the assessor review.

Goal: complete first intake pass by EOD Thu (3 Jul).

Thanks,
Alice Bryant
Security Assessment Lead
FinBank

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
To: Alice Bryant <alice.bryant@finbank.org>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ intake — questions on merge ownership and secrets custody

Alice — thanks for the clear list. We're on it. High-level answers up front:

- Merge/approval model: protected branches require at least one code-review approval from a repository approver group; merge rights are restricted to the Release Engineers team for production branches. PR approvers vary by repo; we will produce a CSV mapping (repo, branch, approver group, merge role).
- CI secrets: secrets used by runners are stored in our Vault cluster (kv-v2). We rotate ephemeral CI credentials on a 7-day cadence for ephemeral tokens; long-lived KMS/HSM keys are rotated annually.
- Audit evidence: we can provide the vault audit logs (redacted service-account IDs), CI job ownership manifest, and the merge-ownership export.

I'll attach the initial artifact exports and a short checklist with owners and rotation timestamps. Jordan I'll need the vault audit tail and the ephemeral rotation summary — can you add those here? Ben can you confirm the PR approvers extract for core infra repos?

Attachments (draft): ci-merge-ownership.csv; ephemeral-rotation-summary.xlsx; vault-access-audit-202506.log (redacted). Also adding links to our SIG ticket and the runbook for rollback.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ intake — questions on merge ownership and secrets custody

Adding the PR extract for the repos Alice flagged. Attached is a CSV with repo->branch->approver_group->merge_role for the last 12 months (generated from our access-control export). Notes:

- Release Engineers have merge rights only on main/prod branches. Other maintainers can approve but cannot merge release branches.
- For services with cross-repo ownership we list the oncall rotation as the tie-breaker for emergency merges.

Jordan — any concerns on delivering the vault audit tail redacted for service-account identifiers? We should maintain the redaction pattern we used for the SOC2 intake (hash prefixes + timestamp window).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Principal, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
(attachment: ci-merge-ownership.csv)

From: jordan.blake@redwood.com
To: Alice Bryant <alice.bryant@finbank.org>, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jul 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ intake — questions on merge ownership and secrets custody

Alice — attaching the vault audit tail and the ephemeral rotation summary (redacted per policy). Quick notes on artifacts provided:

- vault-access-audit-202506.log: truncated to last 30 days, service-account IDs redacted, includes request path, operation, timestamp and result code.
- ephemeral-rotation-summary.xlsx: lists CI job name, vault path, last rotation timestamp, rotation cadence, and current owner.
- ci-merge-ownership.csv: as Ben attached.

Operational controls:
- Ephemeral tokens are minted by the CI orchestration service and expire after 7 days; the token issuer is integrated with our internal keystore and requires PR approval signal for granting elevated merge tokens.
- Canary & revert: we have a documented rollback runbook (link in SIG ticket SIG-412) that ties deployment IDs to a one-click revert; production rollbacks require both Release Engineer and Oncall approval in the incident channel.

Links:
- SIG ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SIG-412
- Runbook excerpt (internal): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0AExampleSharedFolder

If you'd like, we can produce a one-page summary PDF for the assessor that maps artifacts to CAIQ questions. Otherwise these items should satisfy the initial intake.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
(attachments: vault-access-audit-202506.log, ephemeral-rotation-summary.xlsx)
